points.text: Paper difficult to follow.
Experiments not connected to theory; theorems not related back to motivating experiments.
Theory not specific to diffusion; concerns conditional models/classifiers, so text mismatches content.
Diffusion experiment contrived, only to link work to diffusion.
Section 4.1 notation messy and hard to read.
Central simplicity metric R left undefined and unelaborated.
Simplicity-generalization link weakly validated; identity toy ad hoc; no theoretical derivation.
Theory tautological: assumes known separating simplicity metric; no guidance on choosing it.
Analysis uses NLL loss, not diffusion's denoising score matching objective.
Gap between diffusion behaviour and simplified setting; principle not tested on real diffusion models.
Strong convexity assumption restrictive, unlikely for deep networks.
Few experiments; MLP toy far from real large-scale vision or language tasks.
Title and abstract promise foundation-model results beyond low-dimensional parametric scope.
"First sharp" guarantees claim needs qualification.
Empirical section qualitative; generalization not quantified, no criterion or run distributions.
Related work lists LLM papers but ignores simplicity-bias literature.
Duplicated bibliography entries.
Typo "minimizes".
Figure 4 caption vs appendix epoch inconsistency.
Simplicity principle not new; uncited simplicity-bias literature, including negative evidence.
Theorem follows from assuming true parameter is argmin of R.
Theory incremental over Ge et al. (2023).
Vanishing-gap assumption appears unsatisfiable; no example given.
Foundation-model claims mismatch underparameterized, strongly convex scope.
Saharia et al. citation points to wrong paper.
Duplicate bibliography entries.
Diffusion results qualitative; no simplicity measurement; judged by eye.
MLP toy bridging experiment not covered by theory assumptions.
No dose-response test of complexity vs target error across many source-only models.
Who supplies R and why human-expected model minimizes it unjustified; norms architecture-dependent.
No discussion of when fixed-d asymptotic theory approximates large models; framing too strong.
Typos.
Assumption C.3 unsatisfiable for positive-dimensional solution sets; Theorem 4.2 vacuous.
Norm comparison confounded by different training data; argmin-R hypothesis untested.
Foundation-model explanation claim overstated versus stated scope.
"First sharp" supported only for n-rate of constant gap.
Symmetries make Hessian and gap assumptions fail for paper's own MLP/U-Net.
Lambda depends on unknown gap and constants; global minimizer of non-convex objective assumed.
Diffusion generalization shown qualitatively; simplicity unmeasured; number of runs not stated.
Epoch count inconsistency.
Intro tau>0 vs assumption tau>=9.
Wrong Saharia citation and duplicated entries.
Assumption C.3 with tau>=9 incompatible with continuum; Theorem 4.2 has no nontrivial instance.
Section 3.2 comparison confounded by corrupted target labels; hypothesis never tested.
Diffusion model simplicity never measured.
Hessian and gap assumptions fail under permutation symmetry for paper's own networks.
Uniform concentration assumption A.1 fails for unbounded losses like MSE.
Lambda needs unknown quantities; optimization assumed; burn-in never evaluated.
"Sharp" overstated; no lower bound for gap dependence or vanishing-gap rate.
Intro tau>0 vs tau>=9 inconsistency.
Epoch count inconsistency.
Permutation map may assign same center, contradicting text.
No code-availability statement.

P.summary: Theory not about diffusion; framing mismatches content.
Simplicity-generalization link weakly validated by ad hoc toy.
Theory tautological given assumed simplicity metric.
NLL instead of score matching objective.
No validation on real diffusion or large-scale tasks.
Strong convexity assumption restrictive for deep nets.

Q.summary: Simplicity principle not new; simplicity-bias literature missing.
Result follows from assuming true parameter minimizes R.
Assumptions exclude paper's own neural network examples.
Norm comparison confounded; argmin-R hypothesis untested.
Choice of simplicity measure R unjustified.
Lambda oracle and optimization assumed away.
Uniform concentration fails for unbounded losses.
